name: Popular democracy
summary: Popular democracy holds that political decisions should be made as directly as possible by the people, through referendums and other tools for expressing the popular will, rather than by parliaments or officials. It grew out of populism and links popular sovereignty with civil rights, free debate and, in its left-wing strand, economic democracy and participatory institutions such as participatory budgeting. Its answers on most non-democratic questions are therefore thin and split.
scope: The referendum-based and participatory strand described in Wikipedia's Popular democracy article: Leveller popular sovereignty (An Agreement of the People, 1647-49), Rousseau's sovereignty of the people, and contemporary participatory writers such as Hilary Wainwright and Harry Boyte, with Havel's civil-society model. It excludes the label's use by regimes such as Gaddafi's Libya or Assad's Syria, and it does not cover people's-democracy doctrines of Marxist-Leninist states. Many answers outside democratic procedure are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Hilary Wainwright
keyFigures.role: Author of Reclaim the State: Experiments in Popular Democracy, listed as a contemporary popular-democracy writer.

keyFigures.name: Thomas Paine
keyFigures.role: Named among the early thinkers in the popular-democracy tradition.

sources.title: Popular democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, strands, thinkers, listed values (civil rights, economic democracy, anti-partisanship) and criticisms.

sources.title: Democracy
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Direct democracy, majority rule, Rousseau's general will, sortition and tensions with minority rights.

sources.title: An Agreement of the People (1647 and later versions)
sources.author: Levellers and New Model Army Agitators; as summarised by the Civil War Petitions project (bcw-project.org.uk)
sources.usedFor: A summary of the Agreement's clauses: sovereignty in the people, reserved rights, religious freedom, no conscription, equality before the law.

sources.title: The Social Contract and Discourses (G.D.H. Cole translation, with introduction)
sources.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
sources.usedFor: Popular sovereignty and the general will; only Cole's introduction and chapter list were read, not Book III.

public-ownership.rationale: Left strands favour economic democracy while the Leveller root opposed common ownership, so adherents split on state ownership.

unions-good.rationale: Wainwright's work on a new trade unionism points favourable, though the article notes limits of popular democracy for unionism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Levellers defended property while modern participatory strands favour economic democracy, so the movement is split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Economic democracy is listed among the values; collective worker ownership is one form but is not specified.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Free speech is a listed value but equality before the law is too; the sources do not resolve the tension.

state-harmful.rationale: Wainwright's aim is to reclaim and democratize the state, not abolish it, and popular sovereignty presupposes a state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Outside the scope of the sources; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Participatory budgeting and civil-society models place decisions close to citizens, though referendums also operate nationally.

traditional-family.rationale: Christian popular democrats and left participatory democrats sit in the same label and differ on this.

abortion-legal.rationale: Christian-democratic and left strands diverge, and many popular democrats would put it to a vote instead.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian democratic parties used the label but the participatory strand is secular; genuinely split.

gradual-change.rationale: Popular democrats seek deep change through direct participation but by peaceful, procedural means, so split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No foreign-policy content in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Popular democracy is built on referendums and civil society, as in Havel's model, rather than armed overthrow; Nepal's Maoists are an exception.

experts-over-public.rationale: The idea that decisions made by general referendum are fairer than those of officials or parliaments makes this a central rejection.

land-value-tax.rationale: No fiscal doctrine in the sources.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Participatory budgeting favours citizen allocation but state direction by officials runs against it; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anti-partisanship and popular sovereignty are listed values; Nepal's Maoists even moved away from vanguard-party reliance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Levellers placed sovereign power in the people, not the King, and a hereditary head conflicts with that.

democracy-best.rationale: Popular sovereignty is the theme, but the sources show some strands praise participation over bare electoral democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: The article defines popular democracy as direct democracy using referendums and holds that general referendums decide more fairly than parliaments.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement rests on popular will being superior to elite judgment and on equality before the law.

political-violence-never.rationale: The core is peaceful and procedural but revolutionary regimes also used the label, so adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian popular democrats and secular participatory democrats disagree.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law resting on the people's own decisions is the core principle; scripture-based law would override it.

military-superiority.rationale: No foreign or defence doctrine in the sources.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equality before the law and civil rights point away; the article notes majoritarian misuse in Sri Lanka.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands accept it and Leveller, civil-society strands do not.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No foreign-policy or reparations position in the sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not an attitude of reform-minded participatory democracy.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology looks to expanded participation, not restoration.

direct-action.rationale: Civil-society movements use protest, while referendum advocates stress formal channels, so split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivism has no place in the referendum and civil-society traditions the sources describe.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Utopian abolition of specialization is absent from the sources, which describe reformist participatory institutions.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Nepalese Maoist version is described as non-elitist with less reliance on vanguard parties, which is inconsistent with this.

taxation-theft.rationale: Participatory budgeting assumes public revenue allocated democratically.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rousseau grounds legitimacy in the collective body, though civil rights are also listed; split but leaning no.

conscription.rationale: The 1647 Agreement barred pressing men into service, yet republican strands accept citizen obligation; split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement's whole point is that voice through voting outweighs exit; Rousseau treats the right to vote as the citizen's essential part.

total-state.rationale: Civil rights and free debate are listed values, and popular democracy is opposed to a state directing every area of life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: No stated expansionism; civil-society strands reject it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Levellers anchored authority in the people's agreement rather than personal oaths to lords.

bound-labor.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law, as in the 1649 Agreement, rules out legally bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The sources on popular democracy take no epistemological stance on knowledge and power.

single-common-good.rationale: Rousseau's general will points to one common good, whereas pluralist participatory strands treat interests as competing.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy is listed as a value of popular democracy and participatory decisions in workplaces follow.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal macroeconomics is absent from the sources, apart from criticism of neoliberalism that does not settle deficit policy.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is not covered, and strands that are inclusive or majoritarian would answer differently.

class-collaboration.rationale: Christian-democratic strand agrees, left strand disagrees.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Hostile to destroying cultural institutions; popular democrats value inquiry, debate and civil society.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equality before the law is a listed value, though the article notes tensions with feminism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free media are listed values that exclude racial classification by law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands accept it; civil-society strands treat the state as reclaimable, so split.

elite-replacement.rationale: The ideology is anti-elite but this specific conspiracy claim is not part of it.

national-mission.rationale: No mission doctrine in the sources.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminism's relation to popular democracy is noted as limited in the article; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Popular democracy grew from populism, whose core charge is that elites ignore the people; stated as origin, not as a doctrine.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Equal rights before the law and civil rights oppose coercive eugenics.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Economic democracy and participatory budgeting need more than minimal government.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free values are listed as core.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law is in the 1649 Agreement, and equality before the law is a listed value.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Agreement bars Parliament from interfering in religion; free inquiry is listed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strands split between Christian democratic and secular participants.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1647 Agreement declared sovereign power to reside in the people, and its design was a contract between electors and representatives.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are absent from the sources on popular democracy.

population-transfer.rationale: Equality before the law and civil rights oppose expelling minorities, though the article notes majoritarian misuse against Tamils.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rousseau's general will stresses solidarity; Social Darwinism is absent from the sources.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The SEP notes democracy cannot remove its own procedural rights; popular democrats hold both views.

separated-powers.rationale: The Agreement made Parliament supreme under reserved rights, while populists distrust checks on the popular will; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nepal's popular democracy is described as non-elitist with less reliance on vanguard parties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Participatory budgeting is said to raise participation of poorer residents, supporting a pro-poor lean.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The ideology locates problems in institutions and who decides, not demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Equality values oppose this; not directly discussed.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is a direct-democratic device known from Athens, but popular democracy centres on referendums and elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Civil rights are listed as core, though regime users of the label did so.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bias-free mass media and free speech are listed values.

party-commands-army.rationale: Popular sovereignty and anti-partisanship oppose party control of the army.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Leveller Agreement made the people's representatives supreme over the executive.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rests with the people according to Rousseau and the Agreement, not clerics.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Free speech, debate and inquiry are listed civil rights.

recall-officials.rationale: The Agreement conceived the representative as a contract renewed at each election, and recall extends this accountability.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist roots support it, but the participatory strand includes educated activists.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Agreement protects religious freedom but equal application of law is also core.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Agreement of the People was conceived as a written constitution drawn from the people rather than handed down.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rousseau subordinates property to the general will but Levellers defended it; split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereign power resides in the people per the Agreement, which excludes any sacred ruler.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Agreement reserved rights the representatives could not override, and equality before the law is core.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The ideology gives power to the many rather than mixing it with rule by the few.

leader-cult.rationale: The people, not a leader, is the centre of the doctrine, though some regimes claimed the label.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is a Maoist debate, and the popular-democracy sources only mention Nepal's Maoists moving away from vanguard party reliance.

land-redistribution.rationale: Levellers did not seek common property, while left strands might; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Agreement barred Parliament from interfering with religion and free inquiry is a core value.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Referendum logic favours the popular will but civil rights are core values and the SEP notes the tension; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The ideology's means are referendums and civil society.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality of all persons before the law (1649 Agreement) is incompatible with hereditary privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by consent of a people is central; rule by tutelage contradicts it.

patriotic-education.rationale: National loyalty teaching is not covered; populist roots and civil-society strands would split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Agreement reserved inalienable rights from Parliament, and listed civil rights are values of popular democracy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Leveller constitutionalism had the people choose representatives at frequent elections, not inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority decision is the working rule of referenda; the SEP notes Locke treats majority rule as natural.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1647 Agreement made Parliament supreme but popular democracy prefers direct popular votes to parliament.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The doctrine depends on equal citizens, not elite duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Participation is the core virtue; withdrawing contradicts the doctrine.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Political equality of citizens under popular sovereignty argues against ancestry-based rule.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Regimes used the label to claim indigenous forms, while the movement itself espouses universal popular sovereignty.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Popular sovereignty opposes unelected armed guardians.

office-by-exam.rationale: The SEP notes that selection of officials is by election or lot in democracies, and exam-based selection is a rule by the learned.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No economic nationalism is documented; left and populist strands could favour it while civil-society strands would not.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Agreement made representatives a contract with electors renewed regularly, supporting delegates answerable to voters.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Agreement made the elected body supreme, and participatory budgeting extends public control of money.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervening to prevent a people leaving a bloc violates popular sovereignty.

corporate-influence.rationale: Wainwright's strand criticizes big business and neoliberalism, and citizens' influence is meant to outweigh money's.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding rules are not covered, and civil-society values pull against restrictions while sovereignty values pull toward them.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rousseau grounds obligation in the general will and citizens' own consent, so there is a duty to law made by the people.

non-intervention.rationale: Popular sovereignty supports non-intervention, but not the absolute formulation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Critics tie majoritarian populism to such claims, but the doctrine's civil rights and equality oppose them.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Free inquiry, debate and unbiased media are listed values, and informed participation needs public information.

informal-organisation.rationale: Civil-society and referendum strands differ on informal organizing.

religious-nation.rationale: Equality and civil rights oppose a faith-defined national community.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Popular sovereignty denies deference to an external power.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The anti-neoliberal strand favours public over mixed provision.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The sources on popular democracy do not assess capitalism historically.

majority-settlement.rationale: The article cites majoritarian politics' role in persecution of Tamils; the doctrine itself favours equality.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way claims are not made in the sources, though Christian popular democrats sometimes claimed a middle course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The ideology has no stake but equal rights and inquiry values oppose it; adherents on free speech may differ.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Equality before the law and civil rights are listed values.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Free speech and debate are listed civil rights, and anti-partisanship is not suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Agreement barred Parliament from interfering with religious freedom, and free inquiry is core.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Rousseau and popular sovereignty make rule without consent illegitimate.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Authority rests with the people according to the doctrine, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Popular democracy is defined as participatory, direct decision making through referendums and similar tools.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Popular democracy grew out of populism, which often claims to be above left and right, and values anti-partisanship.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist roots in some strands but not in the core.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The equality and civil rights values oppose this claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Agreement states sovereignty rests in the people.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not a position of the doctrine.

rich-first.rationale: The economic democracy value cuts against it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Leveller popular sovereignty rejects inheritance of office, while regimes using the label (Syria) did practice it.

property-franchise.rationale: The Agreement's franchise turned on adult male status, not property, and popular democracy widens participation.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Bias-free media is a listed value; the critique of big business supports it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Agreement set a written constitution that bound rulers and equal law is core.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Agreement and doctrine extend the vote to citizens equally under a common law, not racial groups.

open-government-data.rationale: Debate and informed participation require open information.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious freedom and equality before the law oppose such restriction.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Equality before the law and bias-free values oppose persecution of minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizen assemblies are direct-democratic devices with Athenian precedent in the SEP, though not referendum-centred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Free inquiry and religious freedom oppose state-imposed belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not a position of the ideology.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The SEP notes group representation helps minorities, whereas majoritarian referendum logic differs.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Economic democracy and public participation in budgets favour public provision.

vote-delegation.rationale: Participatory writing treats liquid democracy as a hybrid, which popular democrats could accept.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not a feature of the doctrine.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not a position of the doctrine.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Popular democracy treats politics as procedural collective decision making.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is outside popular democracy, and Christian democratic users of the label split on this.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Equality before the law and economic democracy oppose ethnic economic reservation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nepalese and left-participatory strands emphasise popular power over party-run power.

second-chamber.rationale: The Agreement had a single elected Parliament, while the SEP notes bicameralism as an option.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Equality before the law and anti-partisanship conflict with race-based organising.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal citizenship under a common law opposes separate electorates.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Difference feminism is not covered in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open information supports citizen participation and reduces elite secrecy.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Union-friendly participatory strand, as in Wainwright's Lucas Plan work.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Binding rules constraining popular decisions conflict with popular sovereignty.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Popular democrats seek to reclaim the state, in Wainwright's title, not smash it.

public-service-media.rationale: Bias-free mass media is a listed value.

workers-own-party.rationale: Anti-partisanship is a listed value; left strand might agree.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Hereditary or customary advisory authority in national law conflicts with popular sovereignty.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not covered, and pro-union and civil-liberties strands split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The SEP notes that democracy as procedure is contested between elite theory and more participatory accounts; popular democracy prefers fuller participation.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Free speech and debate values oppose shutdowns.

indirect-election.rationale: Its core is decisions made as directly as possible by the people, and the Agreement of the People and Rousseau put sovereignty in the people rather than in delegates.

missingStatements.text: Sovereign power belongs to the people, who should decide the most important questions by referendum and popular initiative.
missingStatements.rationale: The core of popular democracy per the Wikipedia article is referendums and expressing the popular will, and the Agreement of the People placed sovereignty in the people.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be able to propose laws by petition and force a public vote on them.
missingStatements.rationale: Popular initiatives are named as the central tool of popular and participatory democracy in the sources, with Switzerland the cited example.

missingStatements.text: Participatory budgeting should let residents decide how part of the public budget is spent.
missingStatements.rationale: Participatory budgeting from Porto Alegre is associated with popular democracy by left-wing writers in the article.

notes: Statements on economics, culture and foreign policy are mostly inferred from the left participatory strand; the Leveller root defended property, Christian popular democrats and some regimes differ, so those answers are low-confidence or neutral. The third missing statement rests on the article's note on participatory budgeting; citing Porto Alegre details came from the Participatory democracy article, which was opened but not listed as a source. Fetched summaries came from a summarising tool, not raw page text.
